messages:
cheng: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's autotune rollout I'm seeing a perf regression for long sequences (seqlen > 1024) on some hosts. P99 token latency jumped ~1.8x on A100 (sm_80) clusters. Posting profiler snippet below.

alex: Which autotune commit? can you paste the hash and the runtime flags you used?

cheng: Rollout from 2026-03-15, commit abc123def. Runtime flags: `--autotune=on --kernel-prefer=tensorcore` and we enabled the new sm-aware gating.

maria: Can you drop the microprof output? also does this repro on sm_86 or just sm_80?

cheng: Minimal profiler output:
```
model=redwood-rlhf-v2, host=gpu-a100-12: \
seq=2048, batch=1, kv_cache=enabled
selected_kernel: fast_attn_tc (tensorcore path)
actual_path_taken: bf16_generic
latency_per_token: 34.2ms (was 18.6ms prior)
SM reported: 8.0, tensor_cores=true, bf16_supported=true, fp8_supported=false
```

sam: interesting — logs show selector chose fast_attn_tc but execution fell back to bf16_generic. that fallback cost is expected. why did selector prefer tc if fp8/bf16 support mismatch?

alex: our gating logic currently is roughly: `if (sm_major >= 8 && tensor_cores && !force_no_tc) use_tc_path else use_generic`. looks like `tensor_cores` is true but driver/runtime reported partial bf16 implementation that triggers fallback at kernel launch. driver 510 had some quirks with cuDNN/cuBLAS interactions.

maria: also remember KV cache reduces active attention length. selector uses `max_sequence` from the model config to pick kernel path, not the effective active KV length during streaming. for long prefills + small continuations, we pick TC path but the runtime may end up running a different code path when cached keys are used.

cheng: good catch. repro steps I used: prefills of 1024 tokens, then continue with 1024 gen (so total=2048). KV cache present. If I force `REDW_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=bf16_generic` latency goes back down to ~19ms (weirdly faster).

sam: can you run with `REDW_RUNTIME_PROBE_SM=1` and `REDW_RUNTIME_LOG=kernel_select` to capture the detection vector? that will include `compute_cap`/`driver_report`/`nvml_caps`.

cheng: ran probe. detection vector: `compute_cap=8.0, cuda_driver=510.65, nvml_fp8=false, nvml_bf16=true, tc_perf_est=0.9` — seems perf_est > 0.8 so selector preferred tc. but actual kernel launch failed the bf16 kernel validation path and we fell back.

alex: two ideas: (1) make selector consult a runtime-validated capability bitset (cache the probe result per-device) not just reported flags; (2) change gating to consider `effective_attention_length = max(prefill_tail, gen_len)` (i.e., effective KV depth) rather than model max_sequence alone.

maria: +1 to both. also we should add a lightweight runtime kernel probe at startup that does a quick microkernel sanity check: run a tiny bf16 matmul and validate outputs within tolerance; mark tc/bf16 usable only after that. avoids surprises from driver quirks.

sam: For batching heuristics: if we detect high KV cache hit rate, prefer smaller-token-optimized kernels even if model max seq is large. Batching interacts badly with the TC codegen for very sparse KV shapes. might add a heuristic: `if kv_hit_rate > 0.7 && avg_gen_len < 256 -> prefer_kv_optimized_path`.

cheng: I'll wire up the probe + probe-cache change and add a unit test for the kernel-probe microcheck. also will update selector to use `effective_attention_length`. opening a draft PR now.

alex: please include a simple repro script in `eng-runtime/tools/` so infra can repro on scale. put instructions to set `REDW_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL` and the probe env vars.

maria: add perf regression alert suppression in console until we validate fix, so customers don't get noise. file a rollback playbook too.

perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.internal.redwood/compare?commit=abc123def&baseline=xyz789 — p99 graphs attached. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

cheng: thanks — will iterate. summary action items: probe microcheck, selector-change to effective length, probe cache per-device, add repro script, add console suppression/rollback. I'll ping when PR is ready. :point_up:

alex: thanks, please @sam and @maria on the PR for review. :thumbsup:

maria: acked.
